reader_summary.headline: Guest Paul Cerro stays long Hims despite host concerns about data and competition.
reader_summary.overview: The guest believes Hims' private labs and patient data will drive future growth. The host argues the data is not unique and worries new drugs will hurt customer acquisition. They also discuss why investors struggle to sell winning stocks and look at beaten-down AI power companies.

key_points.text: The guest argues labs and patient data improve retention, which the market currently undervalues.
key_points.evidence_quote: His argument is that labs and patient data are what push retention and LTV up, and that is the part the market isn't paying for.

key_points.text: The host worries new peptide drugs will let startups compete away Hims' ability to attract new customers.
key_points.evidence_quote: And when peptides go legal, I think a hundred Instagram churn-and-burn startups compete away the customer acquisition edge.

key_points.text: The host notes the guest trusts the company's strong balance sheet to win a price war.
key_points.evidence_quote: Paul's answers are worth the hour, especially the balance-sheet argument for a price war and the Ro story.
